synthesis: DEV-2593 addresses Scout user invite/reactivation blockers when a user is deleted. The ticket assumes resend and re-add capabilities are missing, but **resend_onboarding already exists** (introduced in the earlier resend-onboarding hotfix, lines 356-412 of ScoutUsersResource.php). The **real blocker** is email uniqueness: User model uses SoftDeletes, but the database-level unique constraint on `users.email` persists across soft-deleted records, so deleting a Scout user and trying to re-invite them with the same email fails validation with a generic 'already in use' error. Token invalidation already works: each ScoutOnboardingNotification generates a fresh temporarySignedRoute with a 7-day TTL, and the ScoutSetPasswordController guards against reuse after email_verified_at is set (lines 71-73). The ticket conflates three separate flows: (1) resend to unverified user (already works), (2) delete then re-add same email (currently blocked by soft-delete+unique), (3) restore soft-deleted user (RestoreAction exists in UsersResource but needs Scout-context testing). AC 3's 'delete releases email OR UI explains' presents a **critical design fork**: hard-delete Scout users to free emails (breaks audit trail), ignore soft-deletes in uniqueness (requires migration or partial unique index where deleted_at IS NULL), or restore-instead-of-recreate workflow (requires informative error + UI for restore). The sibling password-reset ticket (password reset) is deliberately out-of-scope but shares the same User soft-delete semantics.

scope.summary: Enhance Scout user lifecycle to support email reuse after deletion by either changing delete behavior (hard vs soft), modifying email uniqueness validation to exclude soft-deleted users, or implementing a restore-based workflow with informative errors. Update validation messages to identify the existing user and suggest appropriate action (resend or restore). Ensure fresh onboarding tokens invalidate prior tokens for the same user.

proposed_changes.change: Update new_user_email unique validation (line 140) to either (a) add ->ignore(fn () => User::onlyTrashed()->where('email', '...')->first()?->id) to skip soft-deleted, or (b) add custom validation that detects soft-deleted collision and returns descriptive error naming the deleted user + suggesting restore
proposed_changes.reason: AC 5: already-registered error must name the user and suggest action (restore or contact admin). Current 'This email address is already in use.' is generic and doesn't distinguish soft-deleted from active users.

proposed_changes.change: Similar update to existing_user_email validation (lines 154-170) to handle soft-deleted collision with informative message
proposed_changes.reason: Symmetry with new_user_email path; attaching an existing user can also collide with a soft-deleted email if the admin updates the email inline

proposed_changes.change: Update email unique validation (lines 58-65) to skip soft-deleted or return descriptive error for broader consistency across user management surfaces
proposed_changes.reason: UsersResource is the primary user-management surface; Scout users can be managed from both resources. Consistency avoids admin confusion.

proposed_changes.change: If solution is restore-based: add logic to mutateFormDataBeforeSave (line 54) to detect soft-deleted user with matching email and auto-restore + reassign instead of creating new user
proposed_changes.reason: AC 4: re-enable restores access. If we choose restore-over-recreate, the edit-save path should transparently restore the soft-deleted user rather than failing validation.

proposed_changes.change: If solution is DB-level: drop existing unique constraint on users.email, add partial unique index: CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_email_unique ON users (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
proposed_changes.reason: PostgreSQL partial unique index enforces uniqueness only for non-soft-deleted rows, allowing email reuse after soft-delete without changing application code. Requires migration + testing for Postgres-specific syntax.

proposed_changes.change: If solution is hard-delete: override the delete action to forceDelete() instead of delete() for Scout users, add confirmation modal explaining email will be available for reuse
proposed_changes.reason: AC 3 option A: delete releases email. Hard-delete removes the user row entirely, freeing the email for immediate reuse. Trade-off: loses audit trail + soft-delete benefits.

proposed_changes.change: No change required for token invalidation (AC 2 already met): each notification generates a fresh temporarySignedRoute with unique signature and 7-day TTL; old link becomes invalid after user completes onboarding (email_verified_at guard in ScoutSetPasswordController)
proposed_changes.reason: AC 2: fresh token invalidates prior. Existing implementation already satisfies this: temporarySignedRoute changes with each send, and ScoutSetPasswordController::guardUser (line 71) rejects reuse after verification.

proposed_changes.change: Add test_soft_deleted_user_email_can_be_reused_after_restore and test_soft_deleted_user_email_shows_informative_error_with_restore_suggestion depending on chosen solution path
proposed_changes.reason: Pin the chosen solution (restore-based or uniqueness-exception) with explicit test coverage for the soft-delete collision scenario

proposed_changes.change: Add test_restoring_soft_deleted_scout_user_preserves_kit_settings_and_permission to verify RestoreAction works in Scout context (kit_settings.user_id, clarity-scout permission)
proposed_changes.reason: AC 4: re-enable restores access. UsersResource already has RestoreAction (line 220-224) but no test coverage for Scout-specific state (kit tie, permission).

acceptance_criteria.item: Resend invite for users without password
acceptance_criteria.reason: resend_onboarding action exists in ScoutUsersResource (lines 356-412, introduced by the earlier resend-onboarding hotfix). Visible only for unverified Scout users (line 365-375), sends fresh ScoutOnboardingNotification (line 389), includes success notification + analytics + audit log. Tests confirm (ScoutUsersResourceTest.php:528-551, 555-568).

Each ScoutOnboardingNotification generates a new temporarySignedRoute with unique signature and 7-day TTL (ScoutOnboardingNotification.php:28-33). Old link becomes invalid after user completes onboarding via ScoutSetPasswordController::guardUser email_verified_at check (line 71-73, test at ScoutSetPasswordControllerTest.php:221-251). No explicit token revocation needed; one-shot link pattern enforces single use.

acceptance_criteria.item: Delete releases email OR UI explains + offers Resend/Re-enable
acceptance_criteria.reason: Critical design fork. Current: User soft-delete keeps email in DB due to unique constraint (0001_01_01_000000_create_users_table.php:14), blocking reuse. Option A (delete releases email): change delete to forceDelete() for Scout users, loses audit trail. Option B (UI explains): detect soft-deleted collision in validation, return error naming deleted user + suggest restore via UsersResource (RestoreAction exists at UsersResource.php:220-224). Option C (DB-level): add partial unique index WHERE deleted_at IS NULL (Postgres-specific, requires migration). Needs product input on audit/compliance requirements.

UsersResource already has RestoreAction (line 220-224, filter shows trashed users line 198-202). Needs test coverage to verify restored Scout user retains/regains: (a) kit_settings.user_id tie, (b) clarity-scout permission, (c) unverified state (if deleted before completing onboarding). If validation solution is restore-based (AC 3 option B), ScoutUsersResource should either link to UsersResource restore or auto-restore on collision.

Current validation messages are generic: 'This email address is already in use.' (ScoutUsersResource.php:142, UsersResource.php:64). Must detect soft-deleted vs active collision and return distinct messages: (active) 'email@example.com is registered to [Name]. Contact admin or use different email.' (soft-deleted) 'email@example.com was previously used by [Name] (deleted). Restore the user or contact admin.' Requires custom validation rule or closure with User::withTrashed() query.

questions.q: Should Scout user deletion be hard-delete (releases email immediately but loses audit trail) or soft-delete with modified uniqueness (preserves audit but requires migration or complex validation)?
When a soft-deleted Scout user's email is re-entered, should the UI auto-restore the user or show an error directing admin to UsersResource RestoreAction?
If we add a partial unique index (WHERE deleted_at IS NULL), does this break any queries or application logic that relies on the current DB-level unique constraint?
Should the informative error (AC 5) for soft-deleted collision include a direct 'Restore User' action link, or only text guidance?
When a restored Scout user had an unverified email at deletion time, should they receive a fresh onboarding email automatically or only when admin explicitly toggles Scout access?
Does the ticket claim 'no resend exists' reflect stale ticket intel (scout.md warns this happens often), or is there a different resend flow expected beyond the existing resend_onboarding action?
questions.answer: Stale intel confirmed by precedents.json (resend-onboarding hotfix) and scout.md line 5-12 warning. resend_onboarding already exists and works per tests.

questions.q: Are there any third-party integrations or external systems that rely on users.email uniqueness constraint (e.g. SSO, API tokens, notifications) that would break with a partial unique index?

blockers: Design decision required: hard-delete vs soft-delete-with-modified-uniqueness vs restore-workflow (AC 3 fork) — each path has incompatible implementation. Cannot proceed with code until product/compliance weighs audit-trail preservation vs email-reuse simplicity.

If partial unique index chosen: must verify Postgres version in production supports WHERE clause in unique index (Postgres 9.4+, platform runs 8.3 per PG-021 — WAIT, PG-021 is PHP version. Need to verify actual Postgres version, likely safe but unconfirmed).

Cross-resource consistency: ScoutUsersResource and UsersResource both manage Scout users; changes to email validation must be mirrored or one surface will allow what the other blocks, confusing admins.
notes: scout.md (clarity knowledge card) explicitly warns 'Scout ticket grounding goes stale fast' and 'verify every doesn't exist claim against current main' (lines 5-12). The resend-onboarding hotfix precedent confirms resend_onboarding already exists, validating this warning.

User model uses SoftDeletes (User.php:101) but database unique constraint on email (0001_01_01_000000_create_users_table.php:14) does NOT use a partial index, so soft-deleted emails remain blocked from reuse.

ScoutUsersResource is modeled on Kit (not User), so it has no direct delete action (canDelete returns false, line 502-505). User deletion happens via UsersResource, which has both DeleteAction and RestoreAction (lines 215-224).

UsersResource query uses withoutGlobalScope(SoftDeletingScope::class) (line 228) to show soft-deleted users with red background (line 230), so admins can already see deleted users and restore them. ScoutUsersResource does NOT show soft-deleted users (uses Kit query, not User query).

Kit-user tie lives in kit_settings (not users.kit_id column, which is an accessor per scout-user-assignment.md lines 33-38). Soft-deleting a user does NOT cascade-delete kit_settings row, so restored user immediately has kit tie back (verify with test).

ScoutOnboardingNotification uses relative signatures (absolute: false) and ValidateScoutSignedUrl accepts both absolute and relative (line 22), per the invite-link invalid-signature fix for proxy/TLS-termination issues.

Multiple signed URLs can coexist for the same user (each resend generates a new signature); they don't invalidate each other at generation time. Invalidation happens at use time: after email_verified_at is set, ALL prior links (old and new) become unusable via guardUser check (ScoutSetPasswordController.php:71-73). This satisfies AC 2 'fresh token invalidates prior' in the semantic sense (old link stops working after onboarding).
UsersResourceTest has test_can_see_trashed (line 94-124) proving soft-delete visibility works, but no test_restore_user or test_restore_scout_user pinning the RestoreAction behavior.

The ticket mentions 'cannot re-add user' but does not specify whether this means (a) same user record reactivated or (b) new user record with same email. The distinction matters: restore vs create-new have different implications for audit trail, historical data (activity_log causedBy foreign key), and API tokens (sanctum personal_access_tokens.tokenable_id).

If we go with partial unique index, the migration must use raw SQL (Schema::table does not support WHERE clause in unique). Example: DB::statement('CREATE UNIQUE INDEX users_email_unique_active ON users (email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL'); then Schema::table('users', fn($t) => $t->dropUnique(['email'])).
Filament's unique() validation uses Laravel's Unique rule, which does NOT have a withoutTrashed equivalent. Custom closure or Rule::unique()->ignore()->whereNull('deleted_at') is needed.
AC 5 'names user' requires querying the soft-deleted user, which means validation must use User::withTrashed()->where('email', ...)->first() and check deleted_at to distinguish cases.

No delete capability (canDelete=false line 502).

Lines 54-156 mutateFormDataBeforeSave handles create-new vs assign-existing user paths, grants/revokes clarity-scout permission, sends ScoutOnboardingNotification for unverified users (lines 74-77, 114-116). Entry point for validation changes or auto-restore logic.
key_files.ScoutUserProvisioner.php: Shared provisioning logic for UsersResource's Scout controls. Lines 64-75 extract(), 84-143 reconcile(). Used by both CreateUsers and EditUsers pages. Must mirror any ScoutUsersResource validation changes.
key_files.ScoutOnboardingNotification.php: Queued notification sent to unverified Scout users. Lines 28-33 generate relative temporarySignedRoute with 7-day TTL (AC 2 fresh token mechanism). Each send creates new signature; no explicit revocation needed.

Lines 66-84 guardUser() enforces one-shot link: rejects if email_verified_at exists (line 71-73, AC 2 invalidation mechanism), rejects if no clarity-scout permission (line 81-83). code_flow.resend_invite_flow: Admin clicks resend_onboarding action (ScoutUsersResource.php:356) -> action() callback (line 376-412) checks user is unverified + has clarity-scout permission -> sends ScoutOnboardingNotification (line 389) -> notification generates fresh temporarySignedRoute (ScoutOnboardingNotification.php:28-33) -> user clicks link -> ValidateScoutSignedUrl middleware validates signature (accepts absolute or relative, line 22) -> ScoutSetPasswordController::show renders form (line 17-24) -> user submits password -> update() method (line 27-64) saves password + marks email_verified_at (line 39-41) -> guardUser() will reject future link reuse (line 71-73). ALREADY WORKS per AC 1 + AC 2.
code_flow.create_new_scout_user_flow: Admin fills EditScoutUser form with create_new_user=true (ScoutUsersResource.php:88) + new_user_email (line 136) + web_access_enabled=true (line 183) -> form validates email uniqueness (line 140, ignoreRecord: false) -> mutateFormDataBeforeSave (EditScoutUser.php:54) creates User (line 63-69), assigns USER role (line 72), grants clarity-scout permission (line 74-77), sends ScoutOnboardingNotification if web_access_enabled (line 76) -> KitSettings::updateOrCreate ties user to kit (line 133-139). BLOCKS if email is soft-deleted due to unique constraint.
code_flow.assign_existing_user_flow: Admin fills EditScoutUser form with create_new_user=false + assigned_user_id (ScoutUsersResource.php:96) + web_access_enabled=true -> form validates existing_user_email uniqueness (line 154-170, custom closure) -> mutateFormDataBeforeSave (EditScoutUser.php:84-123) updates email/phone if changed (line 90-99), grants clarity-scout permission if toggled on (line 111-116), sends ScoutOnboardingNotification if unverified (line 114-116) -> KitSettings::updateOrCreate ties user to kit (line 133-139).
code_flow.delete_then_re_add_flow: Admin deletes user via UsersResource DeleteAction (line 215) -> User soft-deleted (deleted_at set, email remains in DB) -> Admin tries to create new Scout user with same email via ScoutUsersResource -> unique validation fails at line 140 with generic 'already in use' error -> BLOCKED. AC 3 aims to fix this by either releasing email (forceDelete), allowing reuse (partial unique index or ignore soft-deleted in validation), or suggesting restore.
code_flow.restore_flow: Admin views UsersResource with TrashedFilter (line 198) set to 'With' or 'Only' -> sees soft-deleted user with red background (line 230) -> clicks RestoreAction (line 220-224) -> User::restore() called (clears deleted_at) -> user reappears in active list. UNKNOWN: does restored Scout user retain kit_settings tie and clarity-scout permission? Needs test (AC 4).

tables.users: PostgreSQL platform.users. Columns: id, name, email (unique, nullable), org_id, email_verified_at, password, deleted_at (soft-delete), created_at, updated_at, mobile_phone, clarity_user_id. Soft-delete keeps row with deleted_at timestamp; email remains occupied. No cascade delete of related tables (kit_settings, zone_user) on soft-delete.
tables.kit_settings: PostgreSQL platform.kit_settings. Columns: kit_id (PK), user_id (unique, nullable, FK to users.id), vehicle_type, timestamps. 1:1 kit-to-user tie. Soft-deleting user does NOT null out kit_settings.user_id (no cascade), so restored user immediately regains kit tie (verify with test). Migration: 2026_04_29_000000_create_kit_settings_table.php.
tables.model_has_permissions: Spatie permissions pivot (team-scoped). Links users to permissions (clarity-scout). Soft-deleting user does NOT revoke permissions (rows persist), so restored user should retain clarity-scout permission (verify with test).
tables.personal_access_tokens: Sanctum tokens table (tokenable_type=User, tokenable_id=user.id). If user is soft-deleted then re-created with same email (new id), old tokens become orphaned. If user is restored (same id), tokens remain valid. Affects AC 3 decision: restore preserves token continuity, create-new does not.

related_components.ValidateScoutSignedUrl: Middleware for scout.set-password route. Validates both absolute and relative signatures (line 22). Renders friendly error view (auth.scout.invalid-link) instead of bare 403 for invalid/expired links (line 30-32). Introduced by the invite-link invalid-signature work to handle signature mismatches behind TLS proxies.

No soft-delete trait. updateOrCreate pattern (ScoutUsersResource EditScoutUser line 133, ScoutUserProvisioner line 131) enforces 1:1 by clearing other kits tied to the same user (line 128-130).

pg_tables: users (read/write): email uniqueness validation queries (withTrashed or not), user creation/update, soft-delete/restore. If partial unique index chosen, ALTER TABLE to drop unique constraint + CREATE UNIQUE INDEX with WHERE clause.

kit_settings (read/write): updateOrCreate when Scout user is created/assigned (lines tied to user_id). No cascade delete on user soft-delete, so restored user regains kit tie automatically (verify orphan cleanup not needed).

model_has_permissions (read/write via Spatie): givePermissionTo/revokePermissionTo for clarity-scout. Soft-deleting user does NOT cascade-delete permission rows, so restored user retains permission (verify with test).

zone_user (read indirectly): Scout users can be assigned to zones. Soft-deleting user may leave orphaned zone_user rows (no cascade delete observed). Restored user may regain zone assignments automatically or may need manual reassignment (test coverage gap).

activity_log (write): resend_onboarding and toggle_web_access actions log to scout-user log_name. Soft-delete does not cascade-delete activity rows, so restored user's history persists (audit continuity benefit of restore-over-recreate).

personal_access_tokens (read indirectly via Sanctum): Sanctum tokens tied to tokenable_id=user.id. If user is restored (same id), tokens remain valid. If user is re-created after hard-delete (new id), old tokens orphaned. Affects AC 3 decision.
data_impact.mv_or_cdc_implications: None. Scout user management is purely PostgreSQL transactional data (user, kit_settings, permissions). No ClickHouse writes or materialized views involved. User soft-delete/restore does not trigger any analytics-side refresh.
indexes_relied_on: users.email unique index (currently DB-level, line 14 of migration). If changed to partial unique WHERE deleted_at IS NULL, ALL queries using email for lookups remain unaffected (index still covers email column). Validation queries using User::where('email', ...)->exists() will need withTrashed() if we want to detect soft-deleted collision.

kit_settings.user_id unique index (enforces 1:1 kit-user). Soft-deleting user leaves user_id orphaned in kit_settings (no cascade null). Restored user immediately regains kit tie (verify kit_settings row was not manually cleared during deleted window).

resource_envelope.scale_notes: Scout user count is bounded by kit count (1:1 kit-user for active Scout users). Typical org has 1-100 kits, so Scout user volume is low. Soft-delete/restore is occasional admin action (not high-frequency operation). Email uniqueness validation is single-row lookup on indexed column (O(1)). No scale concerns.
resource_envelope.perf_notes: If partial unique index chosen, index rebuild during migration may lock users table briefly (< 1 second for typical row counts). Validation queries adding withTrashed() add marginal overhead (index scan includes deleted_at column, no full-table scan). No N+1 concerns; all validation queries are single lookups.

escalate.reason: Critical design fork at AC 3 (hard-delete vs partial unique index vs restore-workflow) cannot be resolved without product/compliance input on audit-trail preservation requirements. Each path has incompatible implementation and different trade-offs: hard-delete loses history but simplifies email reuse; partial unique index requires Postgres-specific migration and careful validation logic; restore-workflow preserves audit but adds UX complexity (informative errors, potential auto-restore). Additionally, AC 5 'names user' for soft-deleted case raises privacy question: should error reveal deleted user's name to current admin, or only confirm 'email was used, contact support'? Recommend brief sync with product owner + compliance to choose path before implementation. Technical execution is straightforward once direction is set (confidence 0.85 assumes design decision made).
